mechanism_narrative: A continued rise in WORKPLACES mobility lifts nearby lunchtime and after-work spending, so RETAIL_REC will increase over the next four weeks if workplace visits keep recovering from their current level.
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES rises for two consecutive weeks and RETAIL_REC does not exceed its prior four-week mean within 28 days, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT rebounds by at least 3 points from one week to the next, access to shopping districts improves and RETAIL_REC should rise within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises at least 3 points week-on-week
failure_condition: If TRANSIT increases by 3 points or more week-on-week and RETAIL_REC fails to improve within the next 14 days, the mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: Higher RESIDENTIAL staying-home together with weaker TRANSIT suppresses discretionary shopping trips, so a joint increase in RESIDENTIAL and decline in TRANSIT will push RETAIL_REC down over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL is elevated while TRANSIT remains depressed and RETAIL_REC still rises over the following 28 days, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An upswing in GROCERY_PHARM without a matching rise in RETAIL_REC indicates substitution toward essential errands, which will hold retail-and-recreation mobility down over the next week.
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM increases for a week and RETAIL_REC also increases rather than falling within 7 days, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained PARKS rebound above its recent level signals warmer outdoor leisure conditions, which will pull discretionary trips toward open-air activities and reduce RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS stays above 10 points for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: If PARKS remains above 10 for two weeks and RETAIL_REC does not fall within the following 14 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Under tightening restrictions, falling TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility jointly suppress discretionary shopping visits, so RETAIL_REC will decline over the next four weeks when both series weaken together.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both fall week-on-week
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both decline in the same week but RETAIL_REC is higher 28 days later, the mechanism is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL continues to rise while PARKS soften, more time spent at home reduces discretionary out-of-home shopping and RETAIL_REC will move lower within four weeks.
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL rises and PARKS fall for two weeks but RETAIL_REC does not decline over the next 28 days, this hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime, a persistent improvement in TRANSIT above its recent trough restores access to commercial areas, so RETAIL_REC should rise over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: If TRANSIT improves from its recent low but RETAIL_REC remains flat or falls over the next 14 days, the hypothesis is rejected.
